content.en: Land reforms in the **Indian Economy** constitute a vital component of the **UPSC GS-3** syllabus, primarily focusing on restructuring agrarian relations. At independence, India inherited a semi-feudal agrarian structure characterized by absentee landlordism, heavy exploitation of tenants, and extreme inequality in land distribution. The primary objective of land reforms was to eliminate intermediaries, protect tenant rights, impose ceilings on agricultural land holdings, and promote cooperative farming to boost rural productivity and social justice.

title.en: Digital India Land Records Modernization Programme (DILRMP)

content.en: An initiative to modernize management, minimize scope of property disputes, and enhance transparency through computerized record-keeping and cadastral mapping.

content.en: Shifting from presumptive titling to conclusive titling, where the state guarantees title ownership, reducing litigation and boosting credit access.
